digest.component_or_area: LLM provider parity harness and Bedrock provider integration
propositions: A provider-parity harness must measure Bedrock inference profiles against direct Anthropic using the same corpus, parity bar, and epoch-majority aggregation as the landed fidelity_spot_eval precedent, with payload and tool parity as the primary gates.

Both Bedrock inference-profile IDs (sonnet-4-6 and opus-4-8) must be invokable in account 896586841071/us-east-1 before any corpus spend, and a temperature=0 rejection on opus-4-8 must be handled by the existing supports_temperature: False override without sampling-parameter errors.

The paired corpus run must prove provider-clean routing (zero non-Bedrock calls on the v2 arm) and exclude agentic disposable-store arms (completion-verifier, ticket-quality, spec-alignment) to ensure only the model variable differs between arms.

Payload and tool parity must be proven by captured outbound requests at the provider boundary, not by code inspection, with system prompt, messages, max_tokens and temperature field-by-field equivalent and all 6 tools identical across both providers and both class slots.

The measured decision-level flips and verdict agreement numbers are informational evidence, not acceptance gates, because comparing two different models' judgements is out of scope; the epic's scope is that the same payloads and tools reach the LLM regardless of provider.

All acceptance criteria must be verified against merged code with offline tests that prove the harness works with zero credentials, zero network calls, and no CI invocation, and the operator must attest the live paired run outcome and re-score the already-recorded results when upstream parity metrics are corrected.
